Coinbase Reveals COIN Buybacks as It Capitalizes on AI

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (395 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that the company is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.
  • "Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.
  • The organization is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that the company is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.

"Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.

The organization is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases. He didn't specify the number of COIN shares, the price or the amount spent.

According to recent reports, at the start of the quarter, Coinbase had $1.96 billion left to repurchase stock. Over the prior three months, it repurchased 37,995 shares for a total cost of $5.3 million, at an average price of $139.91. All repurchases occurred in August, according to its third-quarter report.

Coinbase's board of directors initially authorized stock buybacks of up to $1 billion in October 2024. A year later, the buyback authorization was doubled. The tech giant also received an option to repurchase some outstanding debt.

The board increased the buyback limit again in January 2026, bringing the total authorization to $4 billion.

Some buybacks have been carried out to cancel stock issued as employee compensation. By the end of September, the manufacturer had repurchased 10.2 million Class A shares and canceled more than 85% of the stock issued for employee compensation since the fourth quarter of 2024. This is according to an earnings presentation.

Armstrong envisions a scenario where crypto and AI are involved in different aspects of the same transaction.

For example, AI agents might help users make financial decisions and follow their instructions. Then, a crypto network may be used to transfer funds.

Coinbase wants to provide accounts, payment services, and marketplaces for humans and AI agents to use.

"With AI, everybody has a private banker in your pocket that can help you make better financial decisions," Armstrong posted on Nov. 25.

Sources indicate that coinbase added its wallet and payment services to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments. This offers a way for developers to build agents on Amazon and allow the software to discover paid services. Agents can make small payments when necessary.

Now Armstrong is inviting developers to add their specialized AI models to Agentic.Market.

According to recent reports, according to Armstrong, an AI agent can choose which specialist to hire for a task based on its capabilities and price. Coinbase provides the platform where agents can find specialists and pay them.

China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong.
  • In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight.
  • The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.

In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

The CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

The program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC indicated a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

In a recent development, the obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL introduced its aviation unit.

Sources indicate that CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

According to recent reports, COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, New York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

Heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

Industry observers note that for years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

Look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

And this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

Industry observers note that china also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

  • This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Official XRP Ledger's repository account received a proposed fix to keep only transaction-independent offer removals after a tec that should address the disappearance of failed transactions.

This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back. In some circumstances, offers can be removed when a "tec" failure occurs, even though the transaction that triggered it never succeeded.

In one scenario, a trader could have an existing offer removed before they’re able to add a replacement (for instance, if they don’t have enough reserve to add a upcoming offer). In another, a more complicated Flow could temporarily leave an offer unfunded, only to have funds restored if a subsequent step fails, again resulting in an offer being removed even though the transaction that triggered it failed.

According to recent reports, to address this glitch, rippled will attempt to remove offers that were marked for removal upon tec failure any time a tec failure occurs. Previously, this was attempted for certain tec error codes but not others, with some additional restrictions around Flow-related offer removals (an offer will only be marked for removal if the owner’s balance has not changed in any relevant ways during the course of the Flow).

Offers that have already expired can still be removed, but offers owned by the transactor will be skipped. This is a best effort to make sure offers are consistently added/removed from the order book and should reduce confusing trade results.

Offers to/from regular XRP accounts and balances, XRP sends are unaffected and there are no proposed API changes.

This does not change XRP supply, fees, transaction capacity, etc. and is unlikely to have any effect on XRPL usage or XRP price (other than maybe making XRPL trading more appealing to traders).

This change would mostly affect traders using decentralized exchanges (DEXs) and particularly those using complex/routed/fill-or-kill orders/self-crosses.

Industry observers note that on November 23, XRP briefly hit $1.026 before dropping below $1. Reports indicate crypto selling in general and ETF outflows have been putting pressure on XRP lately. By November 25, XRP was trading at ~$0.92. This software change would not be a catalyst for a price recovery of XRP.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet.
  • “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

Recent findings suggest that chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

“High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the significant bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

In a recent development, “Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is at the moment operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

Industry observers note that while specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the company has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

Industry observers note that those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The big trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

Dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, who is known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, has explained why, in his opinion, no one can predict the prices of cryptocurrencies.

Markus shared his opinion on Wednesday in a reply to an X post with a prediction that the price of Zcash (ZEC) would fall to $100.

"my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except that people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind," the Dogecoin co-founder wrote.

Markus did not mention Zcash or any other token by name in his reply, and his post was about every single cryptocurrency on the market, including the one he created himself.

my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind.

At the time of the post, ZEC was trading at around $728, up by 41.3% over the past year, according to price data on X.

Sources indicate that the latest comment from Markus comes a week after Bitwise filed an S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash ETF. According to the filing, the fund is set to trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC, and it will not stake ZEC or use shielded transactions.

Markus created Dogecoin together with Jackson Palmer in December 2013. The two developers based the cryptocurrency on the Doge meme with a Shiba Inu dog, and they debuted it as a joke about the crypto market of that time.

In a recent development, markus has noted in the past that it took him a couple of hours to write the code of Dogecoin. In 2021, Markus also said on X that he had sold all of his DOGE in 2015 after he lost his job, and that he got about the price of a used Honda Civic for it.

Since then, Markus has stayed active on X under the Shibetoshi Nakamoto name, and he often replies to posts about crypto prices, forecasts and new tokens.

In June 2022, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates spoke about crypto and NFTs at the TechCrunch Sessions: Climate conference.

"As an asset class, it's 100% based on the greater fool theory — that somebody's going to pay more for it than I do," Gates said.

Earlier, at the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting in April 2022, Warren Buffett remarked that he would not buy all of the Bitcoin in the world even for $25.

"If you told me you own all of the bitcoin in the world and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it because what would I do with it?" Buffett noted.

Recent findings suggest that according to Buffett, Bitcoin does not produce anything. At the same meeting, Buffett compared it with farmland and apartment buildings, and he stated that he would pay for a share of them because farmland produces food and apartments produce rent.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An Ethereum ICO whale turned an initial $31,000 investment into $87.21 million.
  • The full investment generated an estimated 2,804x return across multiple sales.
  • Ethereum has fallen 27% over the past month to around $1,641 amid heavy selling pressure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Ethereum ICO whale turned an initial $31,000 investment into $87.21 million.

The full investment generated an estimated 2,804x return across multiple sales.

Ethereum has fallen 27% over the past month to around $1,641 amid heavy selling pressure.

In a recent development, crypto never fails to pay off its long-term holders. An Ethereum investor who put around $31,000 into ETH during the 2015 ICO has finally emptied the wallet, turning an early investment into $87.21 million in realized proceeds.

The wallet’s final sale of 45,000 ETH for $75.35 million closes a decade-long investment that began when each token cost just $0.31.

The investor acquired 100,000 ETH at roughly $0.31 each during Ethereum’s 2015 ICO for roughly $31,000. The wallet later sold 50,000 ETH in 2016 at around $5.47 per token and another 5,000 ETH in late October 2026 for about $2,316 each.

More than 11 years later, on November 26, the whale wallet sold its remaining 45,000 ETH for about $75.35 million, or roughly $1,674 per ETH.

Across all the sales, the original $31,000 investment generated approximately $87.21 million, a return of about 2,804 times the initial amount.

The final sell-off was also split into multiple transfers.

On-chain records show repeated 900 ETH movements worth about $1.53 million each, along with 600 ETH transfers worth roughly $1.02 million.

The activity points to more than one reason for old wallets becoming active, from taking profits and securing liquidity to managing long-held crypto wealth.

The timing is notable because large holders have been making very different moves around ETH.

Lookonchain reports that a separate whale sold 1,107 BTC worth about $86.76 million on Hyperliquid and used the proceeds to buy 34,422 ETH worth roughly $86.5 million, immediately staking the full position.

This mysterious whale keeps rotating from $BTC into $ETH!Over the past 5 days, the whale sold 1,107 $BTC ($86.76M) on Hyperliquid, then bought 34,422 $ETH ($86.5M) and staked it all.https://t.co/1vRa7VBsS5 pic.twitter.com/E0TnJAQvFu.

Other ICO-era wallets have also started moving long-dormant ETH through exchanges, OTC desks, and swaps.

The whale activity comes as Ethereum faces a continuous price drop, with ETH falling to $1,641 and losing 27% over the past month.

Industry observers note that selling pressure has also increased as U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded around $1.51 billion in outflows in November, marking eight consecutive sessions of withdrawals.

Enjin Matrixchain Votes on OpenGov Today: What Changes for ENJ Holders on November 16

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16.
  • It has been revealed that enjin's fresh proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ.
  • Enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16. Here is how the nine tracks, the 1,000 ENJ deposit and conviction voting work, and what the Relaychain vote shows.

It has been revealed that enjin's fresh proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ. It's actually the cheap part.

Enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release. The referendum opened November 10. If it passes, the upgrade is targeted for November 16 at block #12,319,600, with the network moving from runtime 1.3.1 to 1.4.3. Enjin's Fort Canning announcement lays out the plan, and the official changelog carries the technical detail.

According to recent reports, the Relaychain has already made the jump. Referendum #16 approved its upgrade on October 28, and it went live on November 9. The Matrixchain vote is the second half of one upgrade, and it is the half that changes how Matrixchain makes decisions from then on.

Early coverage reported the schedule and the headline numbers: nine tracks, 1,000 ENJ. The changelog and the governance portal show the mechanics behind them, and those mechanics change more than the headlines suggest.

Sources indicate that today, the Matrixchain runs its governance through the older Democracy, Council and Technical Committee pallets, the modules that handle proposals and votes. Fort Canning replaces all three with a new set: Referenda, Conviction Voting, Origins, Whitelist and the Enjin Fellowship. Under OpenGov, any account can submit a referendum on one of nine tracks, and from the moment the upgrade lands, Matrixchain's own upgrades go through that process.

According to recent reports, A track is a lane for a particular kind of decision. Enjin's changelog describes the families: Root and the admin tracks for the highest-stakes changes, Whitelisted Caller for proposals the Fellowship fast-tracks, and two special tracks, Referendum Killer and Referendum Canceller, for stopping a proposal that shouldn't proceed. Matrixchain gets no treasury tracks: those, sized by how much a proposal would spend, stay on the Relaychain, where treasury requests now go. Each track has its own deposit, approval curve and enactment period, and the Enjin Fellowship can fast-track time-sensitive proposals.

Splitting decisions this way means a small treasury request doesn't face the same bar as a change to the chain's core. Riskier tracks demand larger deposits and more support, while smaller ones move faster and cost less.

Industry observers note that the submission deposit rises from 0.025 ENJ to 1,000 ENJ on every track, a 40,000-fold increase. The deposit is refunded when a referendum passes or is canceled, and it exists to deter spam. As an illustration, using the roughly $66 million market cap reported in early October, ENJ traded near three cents, which would put 1,000 ENJ around $33.

That is only the entry ticket. The cost that matters comes next. A referendum also needs a decision deposit before it moves into voting, and the changelog lists steep figures: 2,500,000 ENJ on Root and Fellowship Admin, 1,000,000 ENJ on the other admin tracks, and 2,500 to 250,000 ENJ on the Relaychain's treasury tracks. At the same illustrative price, the 2.5 million ENJ Root deposit comes to roughly $80,000, about 0.12% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance.

Sources indicate that so proposing is cheap, and pushing a proposal through is not. Anyone can raise an idea, but anyone who wants the network to vote on something big needs real stake in the outcome. The changelog notes the same values apply on both chains, and Matrixchain adopts them for its new tracks.

It has been revealed that the best evidence of how these votes work comes from the Relaychain referendum that has already finished. Enjin's governance portal indicates referendum #16 as finalised, approved on October 28 and enacted on November 9.

In a recent development, the final tally on the page is small. Eleven voters cast 381,303.02 ENJ of conviction-weighted voting power, and all of it went to Aye: 100% in favor, 0 ENJ against. The page also highlights raw, unweighted support of 271,303.2 ENJ, which it describes as the total balance backing the proposal and the figure the support curve uses. The conviction multiplier on the page runs from under 1x up to 6x.

According to recent reports, two numbers stand out. First, an entire chain upgrade passed with 271,303 ENJ of raw support, about 0.013% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance, a figure worked out from the portal's number. Second, conviction added about 110,000 ENJ of weight on top of the raw balance, an average multiplier of roughly 1.4x. Voters picked up some extra weight, but most didn't lock their tokens for the long periods that earn the top multipliers.

In a recent development, A 100% Aye result claims little by itself. A scheduled upgrade with no organized opposition passes easily, and the tally shows how thin engagement was.

In a recent development, fort Canning adds the safeguard that thin turnout calls for. A referendum now needs a minimum share of total ENJ voting in support. The changelog sets 0.5% on Root and the admin tracks, 0.005% to 0.125% on the Relaychain's treasury tracks, 0.1% for Referendum Killer and 0.05% for Referendum Canceller. Measured against 2.02 billion ENJ, that means about 10.1 million ENJ on Root, roughly 101,000 to 2.5 million on the treasury tracks, about 2.02 million to kill a referendum and about 1.01 million to cancel one.

Referendum #16's 271,303 ENJ of raw support would clear the lowest treasury floor of about 101,000 ENJ, but it would miss the Root floor by a factor of about 37. The page doesn't show which track the referendum used, and a runtime upgrade typically sits on a high-stakes track, so the Root comparison works as an illustration and not as a finding. The floors also didn't exist when #16 passed, since Fort Canning introduced them.

That is the real change. Under the new rules, 11 wallets can't carry a chain-level decision on their own. Low turnout means failure, and proposals that matter will need far more ENJ behind them. Enjin's changelog says Matrixchain upgrades go through OpenGov starting with this one, which suggests today's vote still runs on the current system, so the floors will first bite on the first OpenGov referendum.

Recent findings suggest that holders who haven't voted can still do so through Enjin's governance portal before the window closes. Voting locks tokens, so the lock length is worth checking first. Enjin's support article on voting explains the trade-off: the longer the lock, the more a vote counts, and tokens stay locked until the period ends.

Node operators on the Matrixchain can wait for the result before upgrading, as Enjin has indicated, and then follow the changelog for the version to install. Relaychain operators already needed client version 1.8.1.

It has been revealed that this vote is more about control than speed. OpenGov spreads decisions across tracks with deposits and support floors built for the weight of each choice, and it moves ENJ holders from voting on a handful of items to a standing governance system. The Relaychain's first vote revealed how little participation it took under the old rules, and the first referenda after November 16 will show whether holders turn out for the fresh ones. If most proposals stall at the decision deposit, the system costs too much. If they clear with a handful of voters, the floors aren't doing their job. Either result will tell holders what their ENJ can do.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie unveiled the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the manufacturer really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” notes Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

Industry observers note that greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

According to recent reports, “Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of major battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The tech giant states the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin, the most valued cryptocurrency by market cap, has seen a massive decline in price value. Since the start of November, the big bull has lost an estimated 23% in price according to data from CoinMarketCap.

It has been revealed that as the asset continues to plummet, market experts are sharing their data-driven analysis, with one such being Bloomberg’s Mike McGlone. The market analyst believes  that Bitcoin could follow the same pattern observed during the NFT market crash and fall to as low as $10,000.

The Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone declared on Sunday that “the everything bubble is bursting,” arguing that broad declines across major assets are already under way after years of aggressive money creation.

In a recent development, in the first half of his post, McGlone said the Bitcoin and crypto bear market since October 2025 “may be a guide of what to expect in most markets, particularly the US stock market, gold, metals, commodities and US Treasury bond yields; they’re all going down. It’s simply overdue reversion.”.

He expects sharp short-covering rallies that “typically gotta keep false hope alive to feed the bear,” comparing many cryptocurrencies to the collapse of NFTs and warning that tokens tracking nothing could approach zero. Bitcoin, he added, may find a “good gravity-pull pivot” near $10,000 to clear speculative excess.

In the second half of his post, McGlone argued that the strong annual gains previously seen in Bitcoin, natural gas, gold, silver and other commodities would reverse and spread weakness into the broader stock market, potentially leaving the S&P 500 with its third annual decline since 2009.

Recent findings suggest that he anticipates significant drawdowns that began from early October highs, lower prices for crude oil and copper, a shift by the Federal Reserve toward easing, and a normal post-inflation period of deflation as US housing peaks. Elevated mortgage rates and Treasury yields, he stated, will later be viewed as an opportunity for investors, with the year more likely to finish in volatility than calm.

Recent findings suggest that “Major green 2026 annual candles in Bitcoin, US natural gas, gold, silver, platinum, palladium, iron ore, nickel, lead, corn, copper, the Nasdaq….will gain contagion with the S&P 500 Total Return ending the year with its third down year since 2009. A 50% drawdown likely started from the Oct. 6 high, a year after Bitcoin’s peak and about 9-months after gold’s top. Crude oil back toward $40. Copper Under $5…” he wrote.

Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Proposal B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.

A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.

The creator of the newer, accordingly more accurate model believes the Bitcoin Power Law is still valid, but the fair value is certainly nowhere near the relevant market conditions.

One way or another, the newer models still set the current price threshold at one of the lowest historical levels in the history of the asset—approximately the 1st percentile of its distribution, which means that it stands among 60 of Bitcoin's daily closes that fell below this threshold.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced model uses a completely different method for calculation: Quantile Regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The main difference is that OLS guesses Bitcoin's price trend based on its historical averages, while QR uses specific points in the price distribution, not an average. Essentially, the newer calculation model smoothens out extremes that made OLS less accurate.

Despite the newer calculation and estimation approach, the improved calculation algorithm and everything else, models are estimating, not making solid predictions.

There are thousands of other factors to consider when determining Bitcoin's next move, so any kind of model is useful only for evaluating the momentum and historical significance of the most recent movements.

It has been revealed that the model also places its 0.1 percentile at $55,185, a level below which Bitcoin has closed only six times. The creator argues that only the lower part of Bitcoin's price distribution, between the 0.1 and 5th percentiles, may continue following the Power Law, while higher levels gradually move down towards this lower boundary.

The model also uses Protocol Time instead of Calendar Time. Still, its creator maintains that the Power Law is not broken. The problem, according to this view, is how previous models measured it and how much they allowed market bubbles to influence the results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple has once again landed a major partnership in Türkiye, but this time around with one of the country’s largest private banks, putting XRP in the spotlight.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm announced it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

This way, Yapı Kredi will have access to adequate security and control it needs to manage all digital assets on behalf of its customers, boosting its security.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider right now supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

It is key to note that Türkiye right now stands as one of the world's top 10 retail crypto markets, with XRP recorded as one of its most widely used cryptocurrencies.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open newly introduced opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia’s reported decision to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia has raised fresh concerns about the global AI infrastructure boom.
  • Beyond Nvidia, the disruption could affect cloud providers, chip suppliers and data centre operators, particularly as billions of dollars in infrastructure financing face closer scrutiny.
  • Sources indicate that nvidia has reportedly instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer, to pause shipments of servers containing its processors to four Southeast Asian countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s reported decision to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia has raised fresh concerns about the global AI infrastructure boom. The move follows tighter US export controls aimed at restricting China’s access to advanced computing chips through overseas data centres.

Beyond Nvidia, the disruption could affect cloud providers, chip suppliers and data centre operators, particularly as billions of dollars in infrastructure financing face closer scrutiny. The development puts AI stocks back under pressure.

Sources indicate that nvidia has reportedly instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer, to pause shipments of servers containing its processors to four Southeast Asian countries. The affected markets are Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

JUST IN: *Nvidia ($NVDA) halts all chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

It has been revealed that the move follows newly introduced US export controls designed to prevent advanced AI chips from reaching restricted Chinese entities through third-party markets. Under the updated rules, exports of certain advanced computing products to the four countries require US government licences.

It has been revealed that southeast Asia has become an notable part of the global AI supply chain. Chinese technology companies have increasingly relied on regional cloud providers and data centre operators to access computing capacity powered by Nvidia processors, particularly as direct access to advanced US chips remains restricted.

The reported shipment pause reflects the growing compliance pressure on manufacturers and distributors. Nvidia and its partners are reportedly working through the requirements, but it remains unclear whether the restrictions will be temporary or lead to longer-term shipment delays.

The export restrictions are also affecting the financing environment for AI infrastructure projects across Asia. Lenders are reportedly reassessing several large data centre deals linked to companies serving Chinese technology customers.

The figures represent separate financing developments, not a combined pool of cancelled loans. Some lenders are conducting additional due diligence, while at least one bank has reportedly withdrawn from the Digital Halo financing and a fund has stepped away from the GMI Cloud deal.

The concern is straightforward: data centre operators need advanced processors to bring new capacity online and generate revenue. If chip shipments or operating licences are delayed, project timelines could shift, weakening the assumptions behind financing agreements.

Industry observers note that the broader lending market is also showing signs of caution. Loans to Asia-Pacific data centre companies have grown from almost zero in 2023 to more than $49 billion, reflecting the region’s expanding role in AI infrastructure. The fresh restrictions are forcing lenders to reassess the regulatory and customer risks attached to that growth.

The latest development adds another risk to an AI trade that has already experienced a significant correction from recent highs. The pressure is no longer limited to chip manufacturers. Companies operating data centres, supplying memory components and financing AI computing capacity are also exposed to changes in infrastructure spending.

For Nvidia, export restrictions introduce uncertainty around shipment destinations and the pace of international sales. For memory suppliers such as Micron and Sandisk, the key concern is whether delays in AI server deployment could affect demand expectations.

It has been revealed that the exposure is particularly significant for companies such as CoreWeave, IREN and Cipher Digital, whose expansion plans depend on substantial capital investment. If lenders become more selective or customers delay infrastructure commitments, these companies could face pressure on funding costs, deployment schedules and expected returns.

It has been revealed that the newly introduced US rules extend beyond individual chip shipments. They also introduce licensing requirements for certain data centre operations that provide substantial computing capacity to companies headquartered in restricted destinations.

It has been revealed that this creates a broader compliance challenge for cloud providers and infrastructure operators. Companies must assess not only where advanced chips are shipped but also who ultimately accesses the computing power and whether those end people require regulatory approval.

For the AI industry, the implications could extend across the supply chain. Chipmakers may face more complex export procedures, data centre operators could experience longer deployment timelines, and lenders may demand greater clarity before financing latest projects.

The duration of Nvidia’s shipment pause, the pace of US licensing approvals and the outcome of major data centre financing reviews will be crucial indicators for AI stocks.

If operators secure licences and shipments resume, the disruption could remain a temporary setback. But prolonged restrictions could delay new capacity, increase financing costs and challenge the aggressive growth assumptions supporting parts of the AI infrastructure market.

For investors, the central question is whether the industry can sustain its infrastructure spending as regulatory scrutiny increases. The AI opportunity remains significant, but access to advanced chips, reliable financing and timely deployment will increasingly determine which companies can turn that demand into revenue.

NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • In a recent development, most headlines on NEAR’s newly introduced inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

In a recent development, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

In a recent development, most headlines on NEAR’s newly introduced inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

In a recent development, everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

Sources indicate that the yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

It has been revealed that new tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

Recent findings suggest that the 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics noted the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

In a recent development, two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a newly introduced proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Sources indicate that ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to revision their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

According to recent reports, three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

The Shiba Inu ecosystem may be set for a privacy boost, as longtime SHIB community member and developer Mazrael hints at privacy potential coming to the blockchain.

Shiba Inu's privacy potential draws from Oxbow's Privacy Pools, the privacy design coauthored by Ethereum cofounder Vitalik Buterin, which is currently a plug-in in the Ethereum Foundation's Kohaku wallet SDK.Mazrael noted that Shibarium is now ready for Oxbow's Privacy Pools, with the groundwork already being done.

Recent findings suggest that WOOF 🐶🪖🫡 And it's privacy done the regulation-friendly way. Privacy Pools come from a 2023 paper Vitalik co-wrote: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest users stay private. No KYC, no backdoors, and you can always exit publicly. Two ways to bring it to Shibarium: 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer. Shibarium is ready either way, and ShibWallet already runs it on testnet 🔥.

The groundwork done on Shibarium (Chain ID 109) includes Cancun opcodes, BN254 pairing support for zero-knowledge proofs, CreateX and Arachnid factories and verified PoseidonT3 and PoseidonT4 contracts at Ethereum addresses.

Mazrael shared a GitHub document, "Shibarium (chain 109) support: chain is prepared," which highlighted this fact. Addressed to the Oxbow team was a request: "Hi 0xbow team! We build on Shibarium (chain ID 109) and would love to see Privacy Pools there. We've done the groundwork so a deployment would be as easy as possible, and ShibWallet prepares to integrate it through Kohaku from day one.".

Mazrael explained that Privacy Pools originated from a 2023 paper Ethereum cofounder Vitalik coauthored: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest consumers stay private. No KYC, no backdoors and users can always exit publicly.

Two ways to bring it to Shibarium include 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer.

For the first option, Mazrael has relayed a GitHub request to the Oxbow team, which is currently showing signs of a green light, with Mazrael remarking that "they did the approval thing when we posted basically.".

A 0xbow privacy pool deployment for Shiba Inu will bring 'entry point', 'verifiers', and 'PrivacyPoolSimple' for native BONE (Shibarium's gas token). It will also bring 'PrivacyPoolComplex' for SHIB and other ecosystem tokens later.

The Shib ecosystem would become privacy-complian and ShibWallet would integrate it through Kohaku from day one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zodia disclosed that a breach exposed limited organization details and some client and employee contact information.

The organization mentioned its investigation had found no unauthorized transactions so far.

The incident raises phishing concerns as exposed names and email addresses could aid impersonation attempts.

A crypto custodian can keep private keys offline and still face a security headache. The Zodia Custody data breach exposed limited client and employee information, putting contact details, not confirmed crypto assets, at the centre of the incident.

Zodia detected attempts to probe its systems on November 23 and temporarily took offline software connecting institutional clients directly to its platform. But, the service has since been restored. CEO Richard Clark confirmed the breach on November 26.

In a recent development, the company determined on November 24 that an unauthorized party had accessed limited information. This included organization details and, for a small number of clients and employees, business contact names and email addresses.

In a recent development, but, that’s enough to create another problem. Exposed names paired with working email addresses can help attackers craft convincing phishing messages impersonating Zodia or its staff.

Industry observers note that however, the company said its investigation had found no unauthorized transactions so far. Its custody model keeps primary cryptographic keys offline and requires multiple approvals for withdrawals.

There is no confirmation in the disclosed information that client holdings or wallet keys were accessed.

Industry observers note that zodia has notified affected clients and regulators. The incident comes weeks after Standard Chartered increased its stake to 100%, bringing the custody business into its digital asset operations.

Standard Chartered shares listed in London rose 2.6% on November 26, the day the breach was reported. That market move doesn’t answer the questions facing affected customers.

Industry observers note that the Zodia Custody data breach makes targeted impersonation a practical concern. Clients should treat unexpected messages requesting withdrawal changes or transfer approvals with suspicion, and verify requests through contact details already held on file.

The investigation’s findings still remain limited. But, how many people were really affected, and whether additional information was accessed or not. Also, how the intrusion occurred have still not been disclosed yet.

Bitcoin failed to hold above $64,000 earlier this week, fell below $60,000 and was trading at around $58,580 on Wednesday morning, down 1.97% over 24 hours, according to TradingView data. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index stood at 13 on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that ethereum lost 3.18% to $1,641, Solana dropped 3.72% to $67.86, and XRP fell 2.23% to $0.908 over the same period, according to CoinMarketCap data. The TOTAL3 index, which tracks the market value of altcoins without Bitcoin and Ethereum, was at $621.3 billion. Among large assets, Tron was the exception and traded at $0.3077, up 0.10%.

Recent findings suggest that the combined share of USDT and USDC in the crypto market rose 1.73% to 12.4%. On Tuesday, the Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.99%, and the S&P 500 lost 0.50%. Nasdaq 100 futures were down 2.93% on Wednesday morning, and the VIX volatility index jumped 16.61% to 30.75, according to TradingView data. The yields on 2-year and 10-year U.S. Treasuries fell to 4.604% and 4.848%, respectively.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $231.56 million in net outflows on Tuesday, and U.S. spot Ether ETFs lost another $64.02 million. It was the sixth trading day in a row of outflows for Bitcoin ETFs. Besides, the Coinbase Premium Index has stayed negative for 63 days in a row, according to CryptoQuant data, and Bitcoin has been trading cheaper in the U.S. than on global exchanges.

Sources indicate that on Wednesday, SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) and the Solana Foundation unveiled that SBI Solana Global had commenced full-scale operations. According to the announcement, the three parties completed a series of agreements for a fresh joint venture structure, and SBI R3 Japan now operates under the new name.

The intends for the venture were first announced on July 13, when the Solana Foundation agreed to take a stake in SBI R3 Japan. Solana said on X that SBI Holdings and SMFG bring "$2.3T in combined assets and 80M+ customers" to the venture.

Recent findings suggest that according to SBI, the company will start with use cases in Japan and then expand across Asia and connect with global on-chain markets. SBI listed four business lines for the venture:.

In a recent development, SBI Holdings is one of Ripple's oldest partners in Asia. SBI owns around 9% of Ripple Labs and holds 60% of SBI Ripple Asia, its joint venture with Ripple, and SBI Remit uses XRP for money transfers from Japan to the Philippines. Earlier in November, SBI chief Yoshitaka Kitao publicly confirmed his support for XRP.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan also spoke about Solana in an interview with Real Vision. According to Hougan, Solana could become "a $300 billion chain" in five years if it captures 10% of global stock trading through tokenization. Hougan called it "a completely reasonable valuation.".

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, Binance also debuted spot trading of five tokenized exchange-traded funds, called bStocks, against USDT. One of them, IBITB, is linked to BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and the others include SOXXB, IGVB, ARTYB and FRHCB.

Ripple also confirmed a partnership with Yapı Kredi, one of the largest private banks in Türkiye. According to Ripple, Yapı Kredi uses Ripple Custody to power its crypto platform Yapı Kredi Kripto. In June, the Turkish Capital Markets Board (CMB) approved the bank's application to operate as a crypto asset custodian, according to Yapı Kredi's filing on the KAP disclosure platform.

"With XRP among the most widely held assets in one of the world's largest retail crypto markets, banks are rapidly embracing enterprise-grade custody," Ripple executive Reece Merrick wrote on X.

Ripple also posted all sessions from its Swell conference, held on Oct. 27–29 in Fresh York, on YouTube. At Swell, Ripple stated that 1,700 institutions use its solutions. On Tuesday, AI project Heurist said on X that AI agents had made more than 10 million inference payments on the XRP Ledger, settled in RLUSD through t54's x402 facilitator.

Industry observers note that on Wednesday, charts shared on X indicated Bitcoin completely below the lowest band of the Rainbow Chart, a long-term model of the Bitcoin price. According to Glassnode data, the Bitcoin hashrate is down 8% year over year, and it is the first annual decline since China banned mining in 2021. Hashprice also fell to a record low, according to Glassnode. The market capitalization of Strategy (MSTR) fell to $35.7 billion, and the Bitcoin on the firm's balance sheet is worth about $51.3 billion.

In a recent development, joao Wedson, CEO of the analytics platform Alphractal, stated on X on Wednesday that retail traders were buying Ethereum and whales and sharks were selling. According to the cumulative volume delta (CVD) data shared by Wedson, orders below $1,000 added $132 million since the Sept. 21 peak. Sharks, with orders from $100,000 to $1 million, sold $4.29 billion, and whales, with orders above $1 million, sold $2.5 billion.

"In my view, a sustainable Ethereum bull market will only return when sharks and whales start buying again," Wedson wrote.

The Ethereum Foundation also published the PQAI #1 roadmap on protecting the network from quantum computers. According to the roadmap, the developers picked the Keccak-256 hash function over faster ZK-friendly options such as Poseidon2 and BLAKE3.

According to recent reports, according to CoinGlass data, $362 million worth of positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and 81% of them were longs. The U.S. dollar index (DXY) stood at 103.92 and USD/JPY at 159.25 on Wednesday morning, according to TradingView.

Recent findings suggest that bitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes posted a Bitcoin chart on X when BTC was at $58,773. Hayes wrote that Bitcoin "will retest $55k, hold on to your butts!" On Saturday, Nov. 21, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024.

In a recent development, some traders took the other side. One of them opened a $500,000 long with 75x leverage and called prices below $60,000 "pure heaven to buy" on X.

Zcash holders just got a newly introduced update as the major crypto exchange Gemini has confirmed support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

Scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this update in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM.

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

It has been revealed that in July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini launched support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the latest Ironwood pool, allowing users to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini users can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

November has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The new 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

None of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

Industry observers note that days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.

Latest Update: Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.
  • Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.
  • Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

It has been revealed that after Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) said there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a upcoming video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

Industry observers note that as we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement notes it “will not operate” without the $299 proposal, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

Recent findings suggest that so Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

Industry observers note that the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

“It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

Sources indicate that that’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Industry observers note that tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version highlights up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

Recent findings suggest that what do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

XRP’s price action may be frustrating investors, but popular crypto analyst Dan Gambardello believes the current market turmoil could be hiding a much bigger opportunity.

While warning that repeated manipulation is keeping the Ripple-linked crypto trapped in a cycle of familiar price movements, Gambardello maintains that the broader crypto market is eventually heading toward an explosive bull run. His latest assessment raises questions about how long XRP holders may have to endure the current market games before bullish momentum finally takes over.

In his latest commentary, Dan Gambardello pointed to XRP’s hourly price chart as evidence of what he considers repeated market manipulation. According to him, the token’s short-term price movements have become increasingly predictable, with similar patterns playing out repeatedly rather than allowing a sustained directional move to develop.

According to recent reports, describing the situation as a case of “rinse and repeat,” the analyst suggested that market participants are dealing with recurring price tactics that continue to frustrate XRP traders. This pattern, in his view, reflects the challenging conditions crypto investors face as they wait for broader bullish momentum to return.

Tech Report: COLDCARD bug goes undetected for 5 years despite 15 security reviews: Details

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (489 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinkite, the tech giant behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.
  • According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the glitch affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.
  • Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinkite, the tech giant behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.

According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the glitch affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.

Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.

That stated, the concern stemmed from a software integration error that caused certain Coldcard devices to use a weaker pseudo-random number generator instead of the intended hardware-based system.

Recent findings suggest that this generator produced less unpredictable recovery phrases, making it easier for attackers to guess the private keys and access users’ Bitcoin. Although the recovery phrases appeared normal and passed some security tests, they did not offer the expected level of protection.

Recent findings suggest that as a result, the vulnerability reportedly resulted in the theft of at least 1,789 BTC, worth approximately $114.7 million at the time. As of 18th November, Coinkite had received around 300 loss-related support tickets linked to 242 customer accounts. However, the actual number of victims could be higher.

Recent findings suggest that that said, vulnerability significantly reduced the difficulty of reconstructing affected wallet seeds. According to Coinkite, the affected seeds had approximately 40 bits of effective entropy on Mk2 and Mk3 devices and 72 bits on Mk4, Mk5, and Q devices.

Sources indicate that this was considerably weaker than the originally intended 128-bit security. This allowed attackers to use offline brute-force searches to reconstruct private keys and gain access to Bitcoin holdings without physically accessing the hardware wallets.

It has been revealed that however, Coinkite did address the issue on 31st July and introduced additional security measures in August. Yet, it is still investigating the incident alongside law enforcement authorities and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

Sources indicate that up until now, the company has not finalized a compensation plan. Regardless, it has been advised that the affected owners must generate entirely upcoming recovery phrases and transfer their Bitcoin to new wallets.

This is because simply updating the firmware will not secure previously compromised recovery phrases.

All of this coincided with Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warning that artificial intelligence could potentially discover mathematical shortcuts to break the cryptographic systems protecting crypto private keys.

At the same time, crypto security losses surged 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, up from $763.97 million in Q2, while reported breaches increased from 67 to 107.

According to recent reports, in that, compromised suppliers, delayed patches, and unaudited components accounted for 77% of losses, highlighting risks beyond smart contract vulnerabilities. Lastly, smart contract flaws also caused $569.5 million in losses, while access control and operational failures contributed to another $477.6 million.
