💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.
  • BMW officially opened its latest Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.
  • The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-fresh iX5 SUV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its latest Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-fresh iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the firm’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the new battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the organization is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We stated we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A manufacturer spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

The 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

Industry observers note that it features BMW’s new “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW noted you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW remarked enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

The electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Recent findings suggest that inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a new 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

It has been revealed that this is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s latest iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

Recent findings suggest that by 2030, BMW plans to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, noted.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

The 12 Best Swim Trunks for Men of 2026, Worn and Tested by Style Editors

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SUMMER MAY BE behind us, but that doesn’t mean your swim trunks need to go into hibernation.
  • Recent findings suggest that over the past four years, I’ve tested more than 20 different pairs of swim trunks—everything from legacy surf brands to buzzy newcomers—but Fair Harbor’s have consistently exceeded my expectations.
  • The first thing I noticed: the fabric.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SUMMER MAY BE behind us, but that doesn’t mean your swim trunks need to go into hibernation. If you’re planning to escape the cold for somewhere sunny this winter, a good pair should be in your suitcase. The beauty of men’s swim trunks is that they can be worn in or out of the water, doubling as the ultimate beachside bottoms or everyday shorts. The best swim trunks for men today have a moisture-wicking and quick-drying fabric, four-way stretch for mobility, a flattering length, and an athletic fit. Finding the right one for you can be a challenge, which is why we're here to help. Our team of fashion editors spent the past year trying and testing swim trunks to find options that blend comfort and style.

Recent findings suggest that over the past four years, I’ve tested more than 20 different pairs of swim trunks—everything from legacy surf brands to buzzy newcomers—but Fair Harbor’s have consistently exceeded my expectations. This pair nails that trifecta of being stylish, functional, and worth the price.

The first thing I noticed: the fabric. It’s a cotton-poly blend that feels smooth and broken-in right out of the gate. It doesn’t feel like any of that stiff, swishy, overly synthetic feel you get with most swim trunks. I’m usually quick to write off built-in liners altogether, but the BreezeKnit liner changed my mind. It feels more like a supportive pair of boxer briefs than the usual scratchy mesh. It’s snug (but comfortable on the crown jewels), breathable, and, most importantly, it doesn’t ride up or chafe. I’ve worn it for full beach days in Puerto Rico—swimming, walking, grabbing lunch—and never once felt the need to adjust.

It has been revealed that the 7-inch inseam hits just above the knee on me, giving it a clean, tailored look. It’s an easy middle ground that works whether you’re getting in the water or just wearing it as your default summer short. There’s enough stretch in the cotton-polyester fabric that I never feel restricted. Plus, it comes in seersucker versions, solid-colored options, and other unique patterns. The hidden zipper pocket stashes a key or card without them slipping out, and the side pockets don’t balloon up in the water—something a lot of trunks still get wrong. It’s not a substitute for a gym short, but the fabric dries rapidly for other oceanside activities.

Read More: The Best Shorts for Men.

It has been revealed that I can’t get enough of the R&R Trunk's timeless style, functional fabric, and flattering fit. I love the no-fuss design with a tailored cut that’s not too baggy or slim. Coupled with the flexible waistband, the fit looks great on most body types. It’s available in two inseams–5.5 and 7.5 inches. The latter provides enough coverage and hits a couple inches above the knee for most men (our universal style recommendation for shorts). Though I wore the shorter length on the beach during my stay in Miami because it indicates off my summer leg gains.

Rhone’s athleisure performs just as well as it looks. I’ve sweat-tested the R&R during beachside runs and volleyball games, and found that its odor-fighting fabric kept me feeling fresh. The mesh liner kept my family jewels locked in, without cutting off circulation. A few editors on our style team who have the R&R trunk say that the liner really does have a second-skin like quality. That’s probably because the polyester blend fabric is stretchy, which felt more comfortable than Lululemon’s (also great!) Swim Short. These durable features also mean the R&R Trunk doubles as a decent gym short if you’re in a pinch, and saves you one less thing to pack for a tropical vacation. We love that it comes in 11 colorways, but if you want to go classic, you can’t go wrong with the Electric Blue or Navy option.

Read more: Best Running Shorts for Men.

The absence of liner offers a comfortable commando style, which is why I prefer a pair like this one from Lululemon. I don’t have to be bothered with any mesh material that feels restrictive or scratchy against my crown jewels—I can just slip it on and head into the water. I also love that the minimal design doesn’t scream “swim trunk”, so I can go from brunch to the boardwalk or the pool without having to do an outfit change. It passes as an everyday short, which is exactly the kind of versatility I want in the summer. The polyester-elastomultiester fabric has so much stretch, it performs just as good—if not better—than most of my gym shorts.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve worn this pair for pickup volleyball and quick workouts, and they move with you instead of clinging or sagging out. It also dries fast and doesn't get that heavy, waterlogged feel after a swim, which makes a huge difference if you’re posted up poolside for a while. The 7-inch inseam is short enough to show some quad, but long enough that it still feels put-together if you’re grabbing a drink after. On my 5’8” frame, it lands a couple inches above the knee with a clean, tailored look—not too baggy, not too slim. If you’re taller, it’ll read a bit shorter and sportier; shorter guys get that ideal mid-thigh cut without going full retro.

After testing Proof’s Performance Swim Trunk, we found that it’s easily the most durable short on this list. Our editors appreciate the polyester-spandex blend fabric, which is stretchy, quick drying, and nearly tear proof. We’ve sported this during tropical hikes and extreme water sports, and found that the Performance Trunk held up to just about anything mother nature threw at it. We like the moisture-wicking liner, which is actually more comfortable than Rhone’s R&R short, but we did find it didn’t dry as promptly as Rhone’s short, and is a bit thicker than we’d prefer. Still, those are minor quibbles for a swim trunk as functional as this one.

It has been revealed that looks-wise, the Performance Trunk isn’t the most stylish of the bunch, and it’s not meant to be. It’s available in six solid colors and two inseam options, all of which have a no-frills design. Though we have to say, because of its barebones aesthetics, the Performance Trunk looks a lot cleaner than your typical bulky hiking short. Proof markets this as a multipurpose trunk that doubles as a gym short, and after putting it through the paces, we agree with that claim. While it’s not as breathable as Ten Thousand’s award-winning Interval Short, Proof’s stretchy fabric moves easily through all sorts of workouts.

For your next vacation, you need a dressy swim trunk that can look great at the beach, bar, or restaurant. Enter this one from Bather, which has a plaid-like pattern with complementing tones of maroon and blue. This makes it more polished than your typical swim shorts, so you can easily pair it with a simple polo or the brand’s matching camp shirt and sandals for a foolproof, lunchtime fit in your arsenal. I’ve worn it to a five-star hotel’s restaurant and then straight to the pool for a mid-day cocktail.

The waistband rests gently on the waist, but you can adjust the fit using the drawstrings. Unlike the scratchy net-like liners in cheaper swim trunks, the nylon-spandex blend is silky and irritation-free, so I could wear it for hours and be comfortable. Plus, the 5.5-inch inseam flatters tall and short guys alike. In terms of functionality, the pockets are super deep for your sunglasses or wallet, while one in the back snaps shut for extra security.

Fair Harbor offers so many great trunks, we couldn't help but to feature the Anchor Short, too. It's available in a variety of solids and prints, but we're big fans of the red stripe option, since it has a cool ‘80s vibe that pairs well with laidback T-shirts, tank tops, and more. This style also comes with the BreezeKnit liner—Fair Harbor's soft, supportive alternative to traditional mesh liner found in swimwear. It provides a snug and comfortable feel, while keeping you cool as ice.

Industry observers note that unlike other picks on this list, The Anchor Trunk is available in three inseams. The 6-inch inseam is great for guys who want to show off their hard-earned leg gains this summer. The 8-inch inseam hits the sweet spot between casual and polished, a safe bet if you're unsure which to go for. And the 10-inch inseam is the longest option, ideal for those who prefer a bit more coverage. Plus, its relaxed (not baggy) fit keeps this from veering into Reno 911! territory.

Read more: Best Hybrid Shorts for Men.

Ralph Lauren’s classic style is the most versatile of the bunch—it works as a swim trunk, a casual short, and even a workout short. I’ve worn it for early runs along the boardwalk, knocked out quick leg circuits on vacation, and then jumped straight into the water without needing to change. The 5.75-inch inseam gives it a shorter, more athletic cut that feels mobile and unrestrictive, especially when you’re moving. But its trimmer, more style-forward look makes it clean enough to pass as an everyday short.

It’s made from a lightweight polyester-elastane blend that dries rapidly and has just enough stretch that you can bend down or twist at any turn. The mesh liner feels breathable and supportive, unlike traditional swim trunks. And because the silhouette is sleek and the design is minimal—save for that signature embroidered pony—it pairs easily with a tee or button-down, making it a true wear-all-day option for beach trips, resort hangs, or any summer day that doesn’t stick to one lane.

It has been revealed that sure, this is the most expensive option on our list, but we think Orlebar Brown's Bulldog Trunk packs serious style that’s worthy of its higher price point. The polyester-elastane fabric is designed with a textured stripe pattern, which is very sharp and unexpected—something most guys would shy away from, so you’ll probably be the only guy at the pool rocking it. I wore mine to the beach in Costa Rica, and no one had anything remotely close to this pair; only baggy boardshort-like types.

This one lands mid-thigh at a 6-inch inseam, which is the golden length for most men. It’s not as stretchy as the Rhone pair, but you’re not rocking this for comfort; the Bulldog is all about quiet luxury. When I’m not in the water, I wear it with just about any solid polo or camp shirt for a five-star resort fit. Plus, the gold fasteners on the waist add extra style points, and just look super plush.

If you’re looking for something more surf-specific, the California-based brand best known for its laid-back, surfer aesthetic delivers the Cruise Boardshort. It’s cut from a lightweight polyester-elastane blend that dries impressively fast, making it ideal for long days in and out of the water. The scalloped leg—where the hem curves slightly upward at the outer thigh—gives you a greater range of motion and a subtle retro-sport look. It’s one of those design tweaks that looks cool but also improves mobility.

It’s built to stay put. The double drawcord waistband adds extra security, so even when you’re getting knocked around by waves or caught in a strong current, you’re not worrying about your trunks slipping. It’s a small but clutch feature if you’re actually swimming, surfing, or doing anything more active than lounging.

Patagonia used a creative, cloudy effect across its lengthy boardshort that looks like sun-faded tie-dye you’d find on a well-traveled surf trip. It’s stylish enough to stand out amongst a sea of guys in basic trunks. Like Vuori’s option, this pair falls right above the knee, providing more coverage in case your shorts ride up as you get out of the water. I’m 5'8" and the 18-inch outseam fits pretty long on me, so the fit is more flattering for taller guys around 6’ feet. If you want things even longer, the brand also offers a 21-inch version that hovers over the knee.

In a recent development, despite the trimmer leg, the cut never feels restrictive—it’s got enough room to move without baggy. It’s made with a lightweight polyester-spandex fabric that has a slightly sturdier structure than most of the swim trunks, but flexes whether you’re paddling out or diving a volleyball. I found it dries down quickly between dips, and the double looped waistband ensures it stays secure.

It has been revealed that patagonia’s Baggies Short has proven its durability on everything from multi-day hikes to back-to-back swimming sessions. Our guys have worn this trunk for backpacking through rugged trails, jumping into rivers, and air-drying in the sun—day after day—without wearing them out. The tough nylon fabric resists abrasion from rocks, sand, and saltwater, while the water-repellent coating helps it dry rapidly.

Unlike traditional slanted pockets that can balloon up in the water, this pair has mesh openings inside, so the water flows out and doesn’t weigh you down. Despite dozens of uses and hours in the ocean, we haven’t seen these trunks fade, fray, or lose shape. Our fashion editors found they pair nicely with a string of T-shirts and sneakers for coffee pick-ups or quick grocery runs.

It has been revealed that sometimes, swim trunks with loud designs can be too in-your-face, but Mack Weldon went easy on this pair. It’s decked out with a dotted gradient pattern that adds a visual pop, without looking tacky. Our editors have worn this with a white polo to balance things out, and works as a foolproof fit for beachside lunches. We especially like the fit: it’s relaxed, but slimmer than the Bather swim trunks for a dressier vibe.

Like most of the swim trunks on this list, this version is made with a polyester-spandex flex that offers a lot of mobility. We could maintain a full range of motion through running, squatting and walking. During our testing, the mesh liner didn’t irritate our family jewels either. In fact, it was one of the more comfortable liners on the list.

If you're performing heavy activities in swimsuits, consider doing without liners. Board shorts, for instance, aren't made with liners for more wiggle room and comfort. Otherwise, liners should fit snugly, but should never be too tight or pinch your skin. Built-in mesh liners provide extra support to your down-there and keep everything in place as you move. Since they're mesh, they're also breathable and quick-drying.

Shorts are getting shorter, and so are swim trunks. But you don't have to chase trends. Typically, around 7 inches in inseam length is a universally flattering fit that hits a couple inches above the thigh. Though if you want to show off your quads, you can't go wrong with a 5-inch inseam, either. If you're looking at outseam lengths, 14-inch is more fashion-forward, 17-inch is a casual mid-length, and 20-inch is as full coverage as you can get without wearing pants.

If you're swimming, surfing, or just moving around a lot in bathing suits, Stafford advises stretch as a must-have factor, since it allows a great fit and range of motion in and out of the water.

Waistbands should fit comfortably on your body, and a drawstring may help you to adjust the waist size if needed. We recommend a full-elastic waistband with a drawcord because it ensures you keep your trunks on, even if you’re diving from the high dive. If you’re going for a snap closure, just make sure it’s not too tight with the ability to unsnap after one beer.

To find the best swim trunks for men, our style team, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, spent the past five years testing more than 100 swim trunks in a variety of settings. For instance, we went whitewater rafting in Proof's performance shorts, swam laps in Rhone's R&R short, and sported Orlebar Brown swim trunks at the beach. From there, we evaluated these swim trunks based on their style, fit, price point, performance in and out of the water, and versatility to make the final top picks.

In a recent development, bonus points if they doubled as athletic shorts or hiking shorts. Specifically, we looked for styles that are not trendy or trend-chasing; instead, our picks of the best swim trunks have a flattering fit, provide a ton of value at reasonable price points, and come in styles that will look great years from now.

According to recent reports, the 12 best swim trunks for men tested by our style editors below are all quick-drying, comfortable, and look great. Whether you're planning to wear these to the beach, poolside, or to your weekend lunch, the best swim trunks for men have you covered.

According to recent reports, obviously, cotton is a no-go—it gets way too heavy when met with water. Our fashion team recommends lightweight synthetic fabrics since they dry promptly and are usually fade-resistant to the sun and chlorine. These synthetic fabrics are ideal for underwater wear because they won't get hefty and pull you down when drenched in water.

Poly with the addition of stretch (Lycra, elastane) material is the most common with good reason—more comfortable, forgiving. Some brands use nylon instead of poly because it absorbs less water and does not get heavy as the waterproofing wears off over time, but nylon does not (take color) dye as deeply and vibrantly as poly.

Choosing the right color and print for men's swim trunks boils down to personal style, skin tone, body type, and occasion. If you prefer a more classic and versatile look, solid colors like navy, blue, or olive are excellent choices that can easily transition from the beach to casual outings. If you want something a bit more eye-catching, subtle patterns like stripes or small geometric prints add personality without being too loud. For those who like to stand out, bright colors, tropical florals, or retro-inspired prints make a strong statement, especially on an island.

Your skin tone can also guide your choice—fairer skin tones tend to work best with earth tones and pastels, while medium to tan skin pairs well with rich blues, corals, or reds. Darker tones can pull off almost any color, but bright neons and strong contrasts pop especially well. Body type plays a factor too—shorter guys might benefit from vertical stripes or a shorter inseam to create a lengthening effect, while taller guys can balance their frame with medium-to-long inseams and bold patterns. Athletic builds look great in solid colors and tailored fits that highlight their shape, whereas stockier builds might find that darker shades or micro-prints create a more streamlined look.

According to recent reports, lastly, think about where you'll be wearing swim trunks. For pool parties and resort vacations, playful prints and vibrant hues add to the fun, while sporty designs with color-blocking work well for active beach days. If you're looking for swim trunks that can double as everyday shorts, muted tones or subtle patterns offer the most versatility. Ultimately, the best choice is whatever makes you feel confident and comfortable.

Breaking: DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (638 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Justice Department noted Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets.
  • The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6.
  • agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S. Justice Department noted Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets.

The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing newly introduced charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts.

U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts.

It has been revealed that “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche mentioned. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.”.

Industry observers note that crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts.

It has been revealed that the Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, claims its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims.

Sources indicate that the FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department remarked. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds.

“The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that in the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans.

It has been revealed that the Secret Service noted it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. One of its cases identified a crypto investment conspiracy run from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California over his alleged role.

In Moldova, State Department-backed raids in October shut down five call centers and led to the detention of eight suspected coordinators who allegedly ran fake crypto trading platforms. The SEC said that in the last year it charged three purported crypto asset trading platforms and four investment clubs with defrauding retail investors of more than $14 million.

Homeland Security Investigations stated its fraud cases have led to the seizure or freezing of more than $120 million, including funds held in bank and cryptocurrency accounts.

The crackdown builds on months of pressure on overseas fraud rings. Trump planned to highlight the push against overseas crypto scams in October, and the U.S. government seized more than $580 million in crypto linked to Southeast Asian scam networks in February. In October 2025, prosecutors moved to seize 127,271 bitcoin tied to a Southeast Asian scam operation.

The stakes are large. Citing Gallup, the department said 10% of U.S. adults experienced a scam last year, directly or through someone in their household, and Americans lost an estimated $68 billion to scams in 2025, including crypto investment scams.

The department noted that an indictment is merely an allegation and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

#201884. How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2198 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2198 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that by definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay.
  • Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture.
  • According to recent reports, now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that by definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay. It’s an art form, a manipulation of material to achieve a desired end result that’s aesthetically appealing.

Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture. We talk about sculpting one's back or legs, implying some kind of crafting of muscles, as if treating the human form like a sculpture. In fact, check the group class schedule of any gym these days, and you’ll likely spot the term “sculpt” appear somewhere on the lineup—directing toward some variation of a Pilates mat or strength training class, often involving lower weights and higher reps.

According to recent reports, now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise? Is it a legitimate term or nothing more than strategic marketing language?

The exercise term actually dates back decades, with the first mentions appearing in fitness publications in the late 1970s. “It comes out of bodybuilding culture, which became more prominent in that period […] and you started to see the term ‘body sculpture,’” indicates Natalia Mehlman Petrezela, PhD, a historian and author of Fit Nation: The Gains and Pains of America’s Exercise Obsession. And while there’s no clear record of who coined the term in a fitness context, there is speculation that it may have been inspired by German strongman Eugen Sandow (often called the "father of modern bodybuilding"), who referenced Greco-Roman sculptures as examples of the “ideal” physique in the late 19th century.

In the 1980s, the idea of sculpting your muscles started to become much more mainstream, with the rise of aerobics, toning workouts, and fitness videos, notes physical therapist and trainer Shannon Ritchey, PT, DPT, founder of Evlo Fitness. As instructors began using the term to describe and market workouts designed to shape and define specific muscles, “sculpting” became part of the everyday fitness vocabulary.

Recent findings suggest that the term also taps into something more personal: this idea that we have the power to change the shape of our own physiques. “I think that it really gained momentum because one, it kind of speaks to the artistry of the body or the artistry of fitness. Also, there's so much individual agency in this,” states Petrezela. “It isn't about you just having the right genetics. Instead, you as an artist have the power to sculpt your own body.”.

In the 1990s, however, the revered muscular look brought about by ’80s fitness culture made way for a celebration of thinner, more waifish bodies. “There was—and this is still the case—a lot of fear around getting too bulky,” notes Petrezela. The term sculpting, however, molded into a promise of strength training without gaining too much muscle, which felt more palatable to women who feared such a physique.

“What's interesting is that we've changed the language over the years, but we're still selling women a very similar idea: that certain exercises will create a long, lean, toned appearance, while others will make them bulky,” says Ritchey.

According to recent reports, if you worked out in the 2010s, you probably remember “sculpt” becoming a fixture of the boutique fitness boom. Still, while studio culture has waxed and waned over the last 20 years, the term has only gained traction, popping up across social media and on class schedules everywhere (think Pilates sculpt, yoga sculpt, and seemingly endless variations), notes Laura Girard, CPT, a NASM personal trainer and co-host of the Fit Literate podcast.

Girard speculates that the popularity of sculpt classes may be buoyed by the widespread craving for more community in a post-pandemic world. After all, group fitness can be a fantastic third space. But there's another reason “sculpt” makes for such an appealing class name: It signals a particular kind of workout experience. Girard has observed “sculpt” used “almost like a dog whistle that [suggests] this class is going to be friendly for women and not scary, but still intense,” she states.

There's an aesthetic appeal, too. Petrezela believes the term’s resurgence of sorts has to do with how weightlifting and building muscle are very much having a moment, yet longstanding fears around getting “bulky” haven’t entirely disappeared. “It doesn't hurt that we are in a very, very image-driven moment in fitness culture,” she notes. “We're not just looking at the images in magazines that come out once a month, but our [social media] feeds are nonstop bodies all day—many of which are shared by influencers who have their own looks for how you can sculpt a body that looks just like theirs, or so they say.”.

According to recent reports, if you were to ask 10 different people on the street what a “sculpt class” is, you may get 10 different answers. To some, sculpt is synonymous with a mat Pilates routine, to others it might be a strength-training session, and to others it might be a yoga practice involving light dumbbells. So, can all of these workouts really fall under the same umbrella? And when a class promises to “sculpt,” is that an actual measurable result your muscles can deliver—or a feeling the name is designed to sell?

Industry observers note that according to the experts, it’s largely the latter. “In a world where two things are popular—strength training and being very thin—’sculpting’ seems to be an appealing middle ground from a marketing perspective,” claims Ritchey. “It promises ‘long, lean muscle tone’ without the perceived risk of building too much muscle.”.

She adds that “sculpt” is often used interchangeably with “toning,” which she describes as a “made-up term” that typically refers to changing your body composition (a.k.a., reducing fat and building muscle).

Because there's no single definition, what you actually do in a sculpt class can vary considerably. Still, Girard notes many sculpt classes share certain characteristics: lighter weights, choreography-inspired movements, and a lot of mat work. She also notes that while exercises are often fatiguing (think: that familiar muscle-burning sensation), they’re not necessarily pushing you to muscle failure via progressive overload (which is necessary for hypertrophy, or muscle-building).

Ritchey, who taught a sculpt class years ago, recalls using dumbbells and bodyweight for high reps. “We would do an entire three- to four-minute song of squats and lunges. That’s likely over 100 squats in a row, which burns and feels hard,” she claims. Of course, it’s certainly possible to promote muscle-building with a low-weight, high-rep range, granted the programming is intentional. “But we know that if you could physically do more than about 30 reps in a row, the load is too light to build muscle.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s important to note that a workout doesn't have to maximize muscle growth to be worthwhile. Certain sculpt classes can offer other benefits, from muscular endurance to simply providing motivation and enjoyment of exercising, often in a group setting. But if your primary goal is to significantly increase muscle size or change your body composition, not every sculpt class will provide the progressive resistance training needed to make that happen.

According to recent reports, that’s where experts say the “sculpt” terminology can get confusing or misleading for some people. Girard fears that the language surrounding sculpt workouts reinforces misconceptions about women's bodies and what exercise can realistically change. “Sculpt as a verb is not a thing we can do to our bodies,” she notes. “We can gain or lose muscle. We can gain or lose fat, but that's more the role of nutrition. But we can't control how those muscles look.”.

Industry observers note that in other words, there's no special exercise technique that creates “long, lean” muscles instead of so-called “bulky” ones. Your genetics influence your muscle shape, while your training can affect how much muscle you build. And the workout's name doesn't change those underlying principles.

In a recent development, what’s more, at a time when there’s seemingly no consensus on how to talk about bodies or fitness in an empowering, nonoffensive way, Girard sees the term “sculpt” as potential coded language. While we may have mostly done away with, say, “bikini body shred” language in 2026, she fears that this nebulous term may be subliminally hinting at the same idea.

And while there's absolutely “nothing wrong with having aesthetic goals,” Ritchey stresses, “women deserve accurate information about how to achieve them.” If body recomp is their goal, they would have more success lifting close to failure and focusing on diet.”.

Ultimately, your muscles don’t know whether you’re in a sculpt class or a traditional strength workout. Instead, they respond to the resistance, effort, and progression involved.

According to recent reports, “It’s funny because while all these trends come and go—and we will see sculpt come and go, too—the science never changes,” Ritchey says. “People just aren’t patient enough with the basics, so they jump on the latest trend thinking it will finally be the golden ticket to seeing results.”.

Because “sculpt” has no one definition, the quality, intensity, and overall experience of classes bearing the name can vary widely, too.

Beyond the workout itself, Girard points out that some sculpt classes can come with an unspoken expectation about who belongs in the room. As she’s observed: “These classes tend to be a self-selecting in-group. You may only see one type of body, or one specific outfit [...] That doesn’t mean it’s wrong or bad to be in a different outfit or in a different body, but it sure can feel that way.”.

It has been revealed that of course, there are also plenty of classes with “sculpt” in the name that are fantastic, inclusive workouts. This all boils down to the instructor, methods, and specific exercises they choose to incorporate—along with the type of community they cultivate. And, in many cases—particularly with larger studios or gyms—instructors have no say in what their class is actually called. “A lot of times, they're just doing what's trending to get people in the door,” states Girard.

So if you’ve been curious to try a newly introduced sculpt class at a local studio—by all means, go for it. Just be sure to go into it with eyes wide open, and give yourself permission to stop or pause or walk away if it doesn’t feel like a productive or positive environment for you. Pay attention to how the workout feels, how the instructor coaches, and whether the environment makes you feel welcome. One potential red flag? Aggressive “bikini body” messaging or marketing that frames building muscle as something to avoid. As Girard emphasizes, “It is definitely, definitely is not.”.

Recent findings suggest that as the experts agree: Finding a form of movement you enjoy is the most notable ingredient for establishing a healthy, consistent fitness routine. “My advice would be to ask yourself why you're doing these classes. Is it because you genuinely enjoy them? Or is it because you believe the burning sensation means you're toning and sculpting your muscles? Because those are two very different things,” states Ritchey.

Sources indicate that have a sculpt workout you absolutely love? That’s wonderful, too. Finding movement you genuinely enjoy is one of the best ways to build a fitness routine you'll actually stick with. The vital thing is understanding what you're getting out of it—and whether that aligns with what you're hoping to achieve.

“I want women to feel empowered to choose exercise based on what they enjoy and what actually works,” notes Ritchey.

For someone primarily focused on building muscle, Ritchey recommends treating sculpt classes as opportunities for cardio or simply enjoyable movement, rather than as a replacement for progressive strength training.

It has been revealed that they can even be great options for off days from lifting. “I don’t want to discourage anyone from moving,” she says. “But at the same time, we deserve to understand what is marketing and what our bodies actually respond to. We are all busy and tired and stressed [and] I want women to know how to best use their efforts to match their goals.”.

Sources indicate that appreciate the workout for what it is, understand what it isn't, and choose what works for you. That, in fact, is the true artistry of exercise.

Natalia Mehlman Petrezela, PhD, is a professor of history at the New School and author of Fit Nation: The Gains and Pains of America’s Exercise Obsession. Shannon Ritchey, PT, DPT, is a physical therapist, fitness instructor, and founder of Evlo Fitness. Laura Girard, CPT, is a NASM-certified personal trainer, founder of The Energy Academy, and co-host of the Fit Literate podcast.

Recent findings suggest that kristine Thomason is a writer and editor with over a decade of experience creating content for print and digital publications. Juiced Scrambler Mini rolled out as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky.
  • The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.
  • It has been revealed that the new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable tech giant. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

It has been revealed that the new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

The Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

Recent findings suggest that that setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

According to recent reports, there’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

Recent findings suggest that the bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

Industry observers note that the Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is right now offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The manufacturer claims preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

That price also comes with something increasingly notable in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual company standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, rapidly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

Industry observers note that there’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

When it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

It’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real manufacturer standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

Want to Build Muscle? These Are the 6 Protein Powders Our Editors Trust

📅 14 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3322 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • PROTEIN POWDER CAN be a powerful supplement when used correctly, like creatine or a multivitamin.
  • There are multiple types of protein powder to sift through, the most common being whey protein.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

PROTEIN POWDER CAN be a powerful supplement when used correctly, like creatine or a multivitamin. But finding the right one for your needs is a major task in an overcrowded protein market. Studies show protein powders can help build lean muscle and promote optimal recovery, making them a widely sought-after supplement. It’s hard to find an easier way to make progress toward your daily protein goals than by taking a few big gulps of a high-protein smoothie. But protein powder is not just a vehicle for hitting your protein goals—many powders also contain other beneficial nutrients, like iron, calcium, fiber, and sometimes even vitamin D.

There are multiple types of protein powder to sift through, the most common being whey protein. Whey protein is derived from cow’s milk and is the most widely consumed type of protein powder. In addition to whey, you’ll find casein protein (also derived from cow’s milk but slower to digest than whey), and plant-based proteins (rice, pea, hemp, pumpkin seed, or a blend of these).

Recent findings suggest that overall, the best protein powders keep it simple: They boast a solid macronutrient profile and taste great. While there are other factors that should be in consideration throughout your search (i.e., third-party testing, type of protein, and price), if you stick to those two basics, you’re likely to find a powder you can easily and consistently implement into your daily routine. Do you need to slam a protein shake as soon as you finish working out? No.

It has been revealed that other lists out there have too many picks, in our opinion, and we're only looking to share with you the very best of what we've found. Our in-house testers have put dozens of protein powders through the blender (and shaker) for years, not months, and dubbed these six as their favorites. The same could be stated for the expert nutritionists we consulted with, like Jordan Sullivan, who's worked with UFC champions like Israel Adesanya and Alex Volkanovski. If you’re on the hunt for a reliable protein powder and want the tedious testing work done for you, read below for our top picks for the best protein powders.

I'm a NASM-certified nutritionist who has spent years covering the intersection of fitness and nutrition. I started with input from the Men's Health editors, including Fitness and Reviews Editor Charles Thorp, NASM, Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM, and Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. Our team spent hundreds of hours testing products, interviewing registered dietitians, medical doctors, fitness professionals, athletes of all kinds (some of whom shared their insights below), and our own Advisory Board.

The testing pool started with the top-rated and bestselling protein powders on the market, then was cut down from there. The products that made it into this guide undergo third-party testing, hold an NSF, USP, or Informed Sport certification, and contain standardized forms of protein in clinically studied, safe amounts.

We considered every nutrition label, ingredient list, price, and many reviews from certified buyers. We made and drank hundreds of post-workout protein smoothies as part of our examination process. The list below represents our thoughtful picks of the very best protein powders to help with your gains in 2026.

In a recent development, the brand name doesn’t lie here—Transparent Labs lists all ingredients clearly on the label and unlike some other protein brands, it doesn’t include ingredients you can’t pronounce. Without fillers or artificial ingredients, you’re left with the key stuff: 28 grams of whey protein isolate, only 1 gram each of carbs and fat, and just 130 calories. You’ll also find a touch of three micronutrients (we’re talking less than 9 percent of your recommended daily value), calcium, iron, and potassium. Another perk? This protein powder is sweetened with stevia extract, so you won’t find any added sugar here.

Industry observers note that men’s Health Fitness and Commerce Editor Charles Thorp, NASM, tested the product personally and says, "it was a refreshing surprise to try a product without unnecessary junk in it. The high-protein content of this product let's me hit my intake goals with ease, and also tastes great.".

All that said, Transparent Labs Whey Protein Isolate is sourced from grass-fed dairy, so it won’t be suitable for vegans. And a protein that’s as clean as this one comes with a higher price tag. While the average protein powder on this list costs closer to $1.50 per serving, TL will run you $2.00 a serving. But for us, Transparent Labs’ high protein content per scoop and lack of filler ingredients is well worth the extra 50 cents.

In a recent development, when looking for the best protein powder for athletes of all ages, we want two things: First, we need an all-around solid product that boasts ample protein. Second, we need a product that is thoroughly third-party tested and certified safe for competitive athletes. Thorne Whey Protein Isolate ticks both of those boxes, and it also happens to taste great, according to Thorp.

Thorp didn’t just test this product for this review. "Thorne is one of the supplement brands I have used the most, and its protein powder has been a mainstay in my routine," he claims. And for good reason: It boasts 21 grams of bioavailable whey protein isolate, and just 4 grams of carbs, 1 gram of fat, and 100 calories. With such a low calorie count, you can also mix this powder with other ingredients (fruit, peanut butter, etc.) to create a hearty, protein-packed smoothie.

Sources indicate that "The taste of the chocolate flavor is smooth, and blends well with any fruit or additional nutrition you want to add, or just on its own with water or milk," Thorp claims. "There is a mild amount of sweetness, but it doesn’t overpower. The result is pretty pleasant as far as taste.”.

In a recent development, while the flavor and macros are great, it’s worth noting that this protein does contain gums, which some athletes may avoid. Thorne also costs a bit more than average at $2.17 per serving—but if you’re a competitive athlete looking for a certified product, that extra cost should provide the assurance you need.

If you’ve been hunting for the right protein powder for a while, it’s likely you’ve come across Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey in the process. Optimum Nutrition is one of the most widely known (and used) protein brands—take it from Thorp, who initially started his fitness journey taking Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard. One of the biggest draws for newbies just testing the waters (and financially savvy folks in general)? The price point.

In a recent development, depending on the jug size (the bigger you go, the cheaper the cost per serving), your price per scoop can be as low as $1.06 with the highest you’ll pay for a scoop from a smaller container being only $1.54. How does the brand keep the cost lower than the market average? Thorp explains, “It's not a pure whey protein isolate (it's a blend) and depending on your stomach, you'll realize this fast.” (Sensitive stomachs may want to lean toward a less dairy-heavy whey isolate.).

But if the whey isolate, whey concentrate, and hydrolyzed whey protein blend is not an matter for your digestive system, this is a great straightforward option featuring 24 grams of protein and 5.5 grams of BCAAs. Just make sure you’re mixing with milk or in a smoothie as we did find this powder to have a synthetic aftertaste in testing when we mixed it solely with water.

Industry observers note that if you’ve been to your local health foods store, you’ve likely seen Orgain Organic Plant Based Protein Powder. Thorp can attest, "I first started using Orgain when I went vegan for a few years," he notes. "This was back when there weren't as many vegan protein powder options as there are now. I liked how accessible it was, through both Amazon (usually at some sort of discount) and at my local Whole Foods.".

According to recent reports, aside from being easy to attain, Orgain is also made with a plant protein blend, which provides a full amino acid profile—a trait sometimes difficult to come across in vegan protein powders. The taste is also reliable. Thorp found the flavor lighter than some of the other protein powders he has tested in his over 10 years working in the supplement space. He also noted that it blends better than most vegan powders with a smooth and creamy mouthfeel, rather than a gritty one.

Though this powder packs 21 grams of protein, it also contains 15 grams of carbs and 3.5 grams of fat, which is higher than your typical whey protein. While this may not be ideal for those on a cut, Thorp offers a different perspective: "While it has more carbs and fats than others, that could be a positive for anyone looking to really supplement their diet in a larger way. [This nutrition profile] makes it a more satisfying drink." And with that, it’s notable to note that a full serving is two scoops, so you may need to blend with a little more water or milk than normal to make sure the texture is not overly thick.

In a recent development, if taste is your number one priority, Dymatize ISO100 should be your number one pick. MH Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., also stands by this protein powder. "It's nutritional profile is great," he notes. "That's why this Dymatize is the only protein I use.".

Sources indicate that “The flavor is top-notch. [Dymatize] is among the most consistently best-tasting wheys, regardless of the specific flavor," says Fitness Editor Cori Ritchey.

Ritchey also noted that her sensitive stomach had no qualms with this hydrolyzed whey protein isolate, which is a testament to the product’s hydrolyzed form. Whey protein isolate is whey protein that has already been broken down into smaller peptides for easier digestion, but hydrolysis takes that processing a step further—studies show the absorption level is even higher in hydrolyzed whey isolate.

With 25 grams of protein and only 120 calories, this is a great lean protein option. Just note that there are artificial flavors and gums, which some may avoid for digestive purposes.

It has been revealed that if you’re vegan, lactose-intolerant, or just want to add a little variety to your protein sources, Transparent Labs is pulling through. Transparent Labs Organic Vegan Protein is our favorite vegan protein powder for two reasons: One, it is a blend of pea and rice protein, which studies have shown offers a complete protein (similar to a whey) with a full amino acid profile. You'll find if you decide to go with just a pea protein product, you'll likely still be recommended to take it with a rice product as well. And two, it boasts 15 percent of your recommended daily iron, which studies show some vegans may be deficient in.

Industry observers note that this vegan protein also packs a higher protein content per serving than most vegan powders—24 grams compared to the more typical 20 grams. Thorp tested Transparent Labs Organic Vegan Protein and thinks it’s a great option not just for vegans, but for anyone looking for a different source of protein. "This is one of my favorite proteins around, and it [just] happens to be vegan, for any of those living by that diet or [who are] lactose intolerant. Also, if your diet already has a lot of dairy in it, using this protein powder can help to diversify your intake," he notes.

It is also worth noting that though Transparent Labs Whey Isolate comes in a wide variety of flavors, the flavor options for the pea protein and rice protein products are more limited—just chocolate or vanilla.

Read More: Best Vegan Protein Powders.

There are three main types of protein powder to consider: whey protein, casein protein, and plant-based protein. You’ve probably seen whey protein the most—it’s derived from cow’s milk and comes in the form of whey concentrate, whey isolate, or hydrolyzed whey. Whey concentrate is the least processed form of whey protein, and therefore, contains the most dairy. Whey isolate is processed to remove most of the dairy, and hydrolyzed whey is processed even further for the best absorption of the three, according to studies.

Casein protein is also derived from cow’s milk, but it is much slower to digest than whey protein. Some people even take casein at night, so it has time to process as they sleep, according to some studies. Plant-based protein is derived from plant-based sources like rice, pea, hemp, pumpkin seed, or a combination of these. It can be higher in carbs and a touch lower in protein because of this, but proteins made of a blend of plant sources typically provide a similar nutritional profile to whey proteins. There is no right or wrong answer when it comes to the type of protein you should seek out—it just comes down to what you’re best able to implement into your fitness routine and daily lifestyle.

According to recent reports, A good protein powder typically offers anywhere from 20 to 30 grams of protein per scoop. Plant-based powders often sit on the lower end of this range with whey and casein being on the higher end. You’ll want to consider how much protein you want from your shakes vs. your whole food meals. If you’re looking to use a protein powder as part of a smoothie for a meal replacement, you’ll want a powder closer to 30 grams of protein, according to studies. If you’re just looking to use a protein shake as a snack, that 20 grams range will work just fine.

According to recent reports, while protein is the main character, fats, carbs, and calories are also vital considerations. If you’re looking to build lean muscle, you’ll want a protein powder that’s low in all three—it’s surprisingly easy to find a protein powder with three or fewer grams of both fat and carbs, especially whey isolates and hydrolyzed wheys. If you're bulking it could even be tempting to try a protein powder that's high in carbs, fats, and calories, but you will never accomplish the same quality of nutrition you get out of actual food. Better to focus on getting a quality protein powder and grab a quick real meal when you can.

While all of the products we talk about on this list are third-party tested, this certification is a big factor to consider when hunting for supplements. Many supplements don’t provide third-party testing (protein powders included), and since supplements aren’t FDA-regulated, there’s no way to know if what’s on the product’s label is actually what’s in the product without third-party testing. Be sure to take this into account when considering any supplement purchase.

Your average protein powder will cost anywhere from $1.00 to $2.00 per serving, with most falling right in the middle around $1.50 per serving. The more expensive powders are typically cleaner, boasting all-natural ingredients, no additives, a higher protein content, and thorough third-party testing. The less expensive options may contain more artificial ingredients, have a lower protein content, and/or offer no third-party testing. Compare prices and ingredients across this list (and throughout the market) to find the best value product for your lifestyle and budget.

In a recent development, while most athletes focus on the big three (protein, fat, carbs), micronutrients should not be overlooked—especially if you follow a specific diet (like vegan or keto). Protein powders can be a great source of other nutrients like iron, calcium, vitamin D, and potassium. These micronutrients may be more key to those who don’t get them as much from their regular diet (vegans, for example, often don’t get enough iron in their regular meals). But according to studies, it’s also a good idea to pay attention to these ingredients to ensure you’re not consuming an overkill amount of any particular micronutrient.

According to recent reports, if you’re finding it difficult to get enough protein in your daily diet, protein powders can help. They’re a convenient way to help hit your protein goals—easier than downing four or five chicken breasts a day, at least.

Getting enough protein in your diet can help you build lean muscle and recover better after your workouts. This is thanks to amino acids (the building blocks of protein), which help stimulate muscle protein synthesis. Studies show during muscle protein synthesis, the body uses these amino acids to repair muscle tissue after your workouts—i.e. your body’s way of building muscle.

Industry observers note that if you’re following a solid workout regimen, protein powders can be a great way to sneak in some additional protein on top of your whole food diet. Studies show protein can help you stay fuller for longer, too. But remember that protein powders are meant to be a supplement, meaning you should still be getting most of your protein from whole food sources.

Protein powders can contain additional ingredients—like artificial flavors or sweeteners, fillers or gums, allergens, and/or added sugars—that some customers may try to avoid. The key with these types of ingredients is moderation.

While artificial flavors and sweeteners haven’t been proven harmful in moderation, there isn’t enough evidence on how consuming them consistently can impact long-term health. Gums and fillers should also be consumed in moderation as they can cause digestive issues. Like artificial flavors/sweeteners, there’s also a broader concern over the long-term effects these ingredients may have, but more research is needed. Added sugars—ingredients like table sugar, high-fructose corn syrup, corn syrup, honey, molasses, and fruit juice concentrates—are also best in moderation, as they’re high in calories but offer no real nutritional value. Studies show added sugar should make up less than 10 percent of your daily calories.

Industry observers note that allergens—like gluten, dairy, or nuts—are the only ingredients you’ll want to avoid entirely if you have a specific food sensitivity. Dairy is probably the most relevant one with protein powders as most whey and casein products do contain dairy (even if it’s in trace amounts).

Lauren Keary is a NASM-certified nutrition coach and fitness/nutrition writer based in the San Francisco Bay Area. She is an ex-collegiate rower, and received her M.A. in magazine journalism and B.A. in literary journalism. She has nearly a decade of professional journalism experience and has covered topics all across the wellness and lifestyles spaces.

Her bylines include Fortune, BarBend, Outside Magazine, Evening Standard, BuzzFeed, Modern Luxury, Women's Running Magazine, TripSavvy, San Diego Magazine, Orange Coast Magazine, Fitt and FoodBeast.

When she's not writing or editing, you can catch her walking with her dog and an iced vanilla latte (half sweet) beachside or catching a flight.

According to recent reports, jordan Sullivan has an Undergraduate Degree in Exercise and Nutrition Science, and a Masters of Dietetic Studies. Jordan is founder of The Fight Dietitian, where he and his team work with World Champion Fighters, Olympians, and top CEOs. Over the years, Jordan has handled the performance nutrition for a number of UFC champions, including Israel Adeanya, Alexander Volkanovski, and Leon Edwards.

According to recent reports, charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. Following an early life in athletics, Charles became a NASM-certified trainer and began writing programs alongside the most respected coaches in the world. Since entering the world of fitness content, Charles has had the opportunity to learn from and train alongside high performance individuals from the NFL, UFC, NBA, Formula 1, CrossFit, US Olympics, and Navy SEALs. When he’s not writing about training programs or gear, he can be seen at the gym or in the wild, putting them to the test.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Woodland version is bigger and more powerful than the standard Toyota bZ, and it may be a better deal right now.

Toyota now sells three electric SUVs in the US (see which one is the best fit for you): the bZ (previously called the bZ4Z), C-HR, and bZ Woodland.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is at the moment offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

The deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota said that if you finance a new 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

In comparison, the standard 2026 bZ is available with 1.99% interest for 72 months at $14.75 for every $1,000 financed.

In a recent development, for leasing, the standard 2026 Toyota bZ is cheaper, starting at $369 per month. The deal is for a 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing for an effective cost of $490 per month.

However, that’s for the single-motor FWD version. Upgrading to AWD will cost around $606 a month for the same 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing.

Toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

In a recent development, toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Sources indicate that although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

In comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

Which one would you choose? The standard Toyota bZ or the bZ Woodland? Let us know in the comments.

Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb stated Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses.
  • The exchange also stated the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month.
  • In a recent development, in an updated notice posted Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb stated Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses.

The exchange also stated the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month.

In a recent development, in an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the newly introduced findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29.

It has been revealed that bithumb now notes an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there.

Recent findings suggest that that is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks.

Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected.

The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers.

It has been revealed that it also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken.

For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets.

Bithumb stated Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals.

The exchange noted it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. It has also set up a dedicated support desk for victims that covers financial and legal counseling as well as compensation reviews.

“We will take responsibility for all harm confirmed to have resulted from this personal information breach and provide all necessary support and compensation to affected customers,” Bithumb mentioned.

It has been revealed that bithumb warned users that it never asks for passwords, verification codes or OTP details by phone, text or messenger. It urged anyone who gets such a request to stop responding, confirm through its official app or customer center and report any financial losses to police.

In a recent development, the disclosure adds to a difficult year for the exchange. Bithumb mistakenly credited people with billions of dollars in bitcoin in February, and regulators fined it $24 million and imposed a six-month partial suspension in March over anti-money laundering violations.

It also comes as South Korea weighs new rules for crypto exchanges, including a 20% cap on ownership stakes. Brokerages including Mirae Asset Securities and Daishin Securities have also suffered a series of cyberattacks.

“We are thoroughly investigating the cause of the incident,” Bithumb stated.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When Jennifer Lawrence joined Instagram in September, fans rejoiced at the idea of seeing more content from the actress known for her sarcastic humor and likable authenticity.
